source.title: InstructionCP: A fast approach to transfer Large Language Models into target language

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses safety and RLHF retention and cites prior fine-tuning safety findings, but its own safety-related results measure toxicity scores, not harmful-request compliance or the other behaviors named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Qi et al. (2023), but those cited findings are not this study's results. Its own ToxiGen scores bear on safety broadly, but do not measure compliance with harmful user requests. The TruthfulQA and BOLD results do not measure the claim versions' named behaviors. No results on response-position KL, prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-localized weights, shallowness mechanisms, or deepening safety are reported.
record.test_reason: The study continually pre-trains LLaMA3-8B-instruct on benign target-language data (orgCP vs InsCP). Its only safety-adjacent measure is the ToxiGen toxicity score (RoBERTa classifier on generations), plus TruthfulQA, BOLD and an aggregate MT-Bench score. None of these measures compliance with harmful user requests. There is also nothing on per-token KL, prefilling or suffix bypasses, safety-localized weights, causes of shallowness, or deepening. The toxicity rise after benign orgCP (TW 0.14→0.26) is near V2 but measures a different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version. The Qi et al. findings are cited, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that InsCP (CP with the chat template) keeps the instruct model's RLHF-related abilities and English knowledge while adding target-language alignment with about 0.1B tokens. They attribute orgCP's worse reliability scores to RLHF ability diminishing during CP/SFT.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares instruction continual pre-training with original continual pre-training on target-language data, rather than fine-tuning on harmful or benign safety examples. It does not measure response-position KL or bypass interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The ToxiGen scores differ by training method and language: orgCP scores 0.12 (EN) and 0.26 (TW), while InsCP scores 0.07 (EN) and 0.16 (TW).

fits_no_version.finding: Benign continual pre-training without a chat template (orgCP) raises ToxiGen toxicity, sharply in Traditional Chinese (EN 0.10→0.12; TW 0.14→0.26). Wrapping the same data in the chat template (InsCP) leaves toxicity near baseline (EN 0.07; TW 0.16). No uncertainty is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign target-language continual pre-training of an instruct model raises toxic-generation scores unless training data keeps the model's chat template.

record.problems: The safety-related results use toxicity-generation scores rather than harmful-request compliance; no uncertainty estimates are provided for the ToxiGen values.
record.rows_left_out: TruthfulQA and BOLD results are omitted because they measure factual reliability and sentiment, not the safety behaviors relevant to the claim versions.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples and no harmful-request compliance rate.
Benign data (target-language CP) is used, but harmful-request compliance is never measured; only ToxiGen toxicity is.
No per-token KL by response position.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding-change attacks.
No analysis of safety-carrying weights or ranks.
Authors hypothesise CP/SFT diminishes RLHF ability but give no mechanism test for shallowness.
InsCP is a language-transfer method, not safety deepening; no attack robustness tested.

record.verdict_notes: The intro asserts 'Our experiments validate similar observations with other LLMs like LLaMA2' about safety loss under non-English fine-tuning. However, no LLaMA2 results appear in the text, so there is nothing to record. MT-Bench scores fold harmfulness into a single GPT-4 score and cannot isolate safety. There is only one run per model and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Per-token KL by response position on harmful prompts.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether the effect persists.
